raw:
The task: a parking app push notification. User is parked at 信義停車場, timer expires in 10 minutes, overtime costs NT$60 per hour.

Rules: microcopy doctrine. Push notification title (s1) and body (s2). No extra clauses, no reassurance, no chat register. State the fact: which lot, how long left, what happens if exceeded.

Let me think about what a push notification needs:
- s1 (title): short, names the state. Options: 「計時即將到期」or 「停車計時快到期」. The lot name — where does it go? Title should be compact. Could do s1: 「信義停車場 計時將到期」 — hmm, spaces? The doctrine says half-width space between Chinese and numerals. 「10 分鐘」 with space.

- s2 (body): the facts not already in the title: 10 minutes left, overtime NT$60/hour. Something like: 「還有 10 分鐘，超時以每小時 60 元計費。」 That names the state and consequence.

Should the lot name be in s1 or s2? Push notifications typically: title short, body has detail. Putting the lot name in the title helps distinguish at a glance. s1: 「信義停車場計時將到期」 — a bit long. Or s1: 「停車時間將到期」 and s2 includes the lot: 「信義停車場剩 10 分鐘，超時每小時 60 元。」

Doctrine: shortest conventional wording, no redundancy. Delete pass: does the user need "停車場"? They're parked; the timer expiring is the key fact. The lot name disambiguates (user might park in multiple lots or have history) — worth keeping once, not twice.

Options:

A: s1 「停車計時將到期」, s2 「信義停車場還有 10 分鐘，超時每小時 60 元。」

B: s1 「信義停車場 · 計時將到期」, s2 「還有 10 分鐘到期，超時以每小時 NT$60 計費。」

The source says 超時每小時 NT$60. In Taiwan, 「60 元」 is natural; NT$60 also fine. Original currency given as NT$60 — keep as NT$60? The rule about spaces: 「超時每小時 NT$60」.

Avoid 約? No estimate here. Avoid chat tone. Status form: closed state for status; this is a notification — a warning/reminder. Form: state + consequence. 「將到期」 is a future state — fine for a warning. Taiwan usage: 「即將」 vs 「將」. 「計時即將到期」 reads well. 「快到期」 is colloquial (chat register-ish). Prefer 「即將到期」.

s1: 「信義停車場計時即將到期」 — 9 chars, acceptable. Or add space between: 「信義停車場 計時即將到期」? Push titles don't usually need that. Keep as one phrase.

s2: 「還有 10 分鐘到期，超時每小時 NT$60。」 Hmm, "還有 10 分鐘" — the remaining time. Actually if s1 says 即將到期, s2 gives the number: 「剩 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60。」 That's tight. 「超時每小時 NT$60」 — maybe 「超時以每小時 NT$60 計費」 adds 計費 clarity, but is that an extra clause? It's the consequence — needed. 「超時每小時 NT$60」 is already clear (overtime costs NT$60/hour). Shorter is better.

Do we need 「請留意」 or 「請及時續停」? No — no coaching, no instruction unless there's an action the user can take; a "加時" button might exist in the app, but the copy shouldn't instruct beyond what's known. Skip.

Also avoid 「喔」、「！」. No exclamation marks.

Numbers with half-width space: 「10 分鐘」, 「NT$60」. For 「超時每小時 NT$60」 fine.

Final:
s1: 「停車計時即將到期」
s2: 「信義停車場剩 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60。」

Punctuation: body sentences get 句號 per doctrine. s1 no 句號.

Check six tests: deletion — every clause carries info: lot name (disambiguates), 10 min (time), 60/hr (consequence). Counter-question — none answer a non-question. Chat — no. Control — n/a. Provenance — no. Affect — no. 「剩 10 分鐘」 could read as lacking? 「剩」 standard for remaining time. Alternative 「還有 10 分鐘」 also standard, slightly softer but fine. 「剩」 is fine and shorter.

Should the lot be in title instead? Some push systems bold the title; having 「信義停車場」 in the title makes the lockscreen glance useful, and body carries numbers. Either works. I'll put lot in title? Title: 「信義停車場計時即將到期」 is longish but okay. Hmm — actually keeping title generic lets it be reused; the body has the specific. Either satisfies. I'll go with lot name in title for glance value? Let me decide: many parking apps do 「停車計時快到期」 title + 「信義停車場還有 10 分鐘…」. I'll do:

s1: "停車計時即將到期"
s2: "信義停車場剩 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60。"

Output JSON only.</think>{"s1":"停車計時即將到期","s2":"信義停車場剩 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60。"}

parsed.s2: 信義停車場剩 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60。
